analysis.title: Macro Volatility Digest: Equity Markets Remain Resilient Amidst Continued Yield Surge
key_insights: Cross-asset implied volatilities edged higher for the week. Cooler-than-expected core inflation and weak job growth briefly slowed the rise in bond yields.
Rates volatility rose again. The MOVE Index reached 110 mid-week, 3 points below its 1-year high, as the 30-year yield breached 5.63%, its highest level since 2002.
Fed Vice Chair Jefferson and NY Fed President Williams made 'dovish-hike' comments that signaled a case for deferring a hike. The probability of an October hike fell from 70% to 20%.

The probability of a hike by December stays around 80%. Fed Funds futures therefore imply that any change in Fed policy is about the timing of the next hike, not a moderation or reversal of the tightening bias.
Corporate bond volatility jumped. Investment grade (VIXIG) and high-yield (VIXHY) vols went from the 6th and 11th percentile two weeks ago to the 79th and 84th percentile now.

Duration risk and credit risk have separated. IG yields rose over two weeks but IG OAS (the credit premium over Treasuries) is still near historical tights, so IG vol mainly reflects the same rate uncertainty as the MOVE spike.

High-yield OAS, especially for CCC-rated credits, has risen over 300bps YTD to 12.1% and is above its 25-year average. HY implied vol is rising because investors demand more compensation for lower-quality credit.

French sovereign spreads widened sharply. The OAT-Bund spread reached 140 bps and 5-year French CDS hit its widest level since the European sovereign debt crisis. Traders are pricing this as France-specific, not a broad Eurozone concern.

Contagion to European equity volatility has been contained so far. French companies are about one third of the Eurostoxx-50, but most are global multinationals not tied to the French economy. VSTOXX rose 2 points w/w to 19.2.
US equity vol, correlation and skew rose on the prior week's hawkish Fed sentiment but ended the week little changed. The VIX closed at 15.3, correlation at 8.0, and skew at 7th percentile lows.

The vol monitor shows rates and credit vol at the top of 1-year ranges. TLT 1M implied vol is in the 98th to 100th percentile and HYG implied is 6.8 against 4.0 realized. EWZ implied vol of 58.8 rose 11.8 points on the week and sits at the 100th percentile.
SPX 1M implied vol is 12.4 against 10.7 realized, a 1.7-point spread at the 45th percentile of its 1-year range. RTY implied (18.2) is 6.8 points above realized (11.4) at the 89th percentile.
GLD implied vol of 20.3 sits at the 10th to 11th percentile of its 1-year range and below its 22.2 realized vol. USO implied vol of about 48 is slightly above its 48.3 realized.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Together with weak job growth, it briefly slowed the rise in bond yields and cut the probability of an October Fed hike.
Added to the case for deferring a Fed hike, though yields stayed elevated.
Drove the rise in rates volatility, with the MOVE Index at 110.
